historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun describes a Berber chieftain named Kadeen, who rose to prominence in the Maghrib during the earliest centuries of Islam. He founded the Awdagas dynasty and extended his rule over the Rif Mountains and the Mediterranean coast. Kadeen is notable for his military prowess and his ability to unite various Berber tribes under his banner. He is considered a legendary figure in Berber history.

The second reference comes from Ibn Battuta, a famous traveler from Tangier who lived during the 14th century. He mentions a city named Kadina, which was a major Islamic trading center located in present-day Mauritania. Ibn Battuta notes that the city was ruled by a powerful emir named Kadeen, who was known for his wealth and his extensive patronage of learning and the arts.
